- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment strength.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (sentiment drops to 0.0–0.27) — adjust downward by 1–3% to avoid overcorrection.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent sentiment — shift forecast horizon slightly backward (e.g., 1–2 days) for smoother alignment.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment is strong.
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >3% in 3–5 days, apply a “cool-down” correction — reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment-driven momentum: if sentiment > 0.7 for 3+ consecutive days, forecast should be 1–2% below true outcome to avoid overconfidence bias.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in the cycle — reduce first 5–7 days by 1–3% if sentiment is rising.
